LC 61 0483S (SCS)
Creating the Senate Higher Education in Prison Study Committee; and for other purposes.
WHEREAS, higher education is a strong determinant of employment outcomes, social
mobility, and future income because it equips individuals with the knowledge and skills
needed to contribute effectively to society; and
WHEREAS, the 2023 overhaul of the Free Application for Federal Student Aid program
allotted federal Pell Grants to people in prisons and increased total spending by $617 million,
giving the nation the greatest opportunity to expand higher education in prison since such
grants were cut in 1994; and
WHEREAS, there are currently more than 47,000 Georgians in our state prisons, which cost
taxpayers $1.32 billion in 2024; and
WHEREAS, the rate of recidivism in Georgia is at least 30 percent, and postsecondary
education has been found to be the most effective educational program at reducing
recidivism with multiple studies finding that education in prison reduces its rate by 43
percent; and
LC 61 0483S (SCS)
WHEREAS, providing postsecondary education to people in prisons will add specialized
laborers to Georgia's economy, bolstering our workforce to remain the number one state to
